text:
What does it take to build a robot agent?

We have VLAs and WAMs as foundation models for robots. But we still haven't cracked real autonomy.

Digital agents use a harness, connecting models with memory, tools, planning, etc. So what if we make the harness embodied and pair it with VLAs or WAMs?

▪️ Grid Robotics proposed this idea as a blueprint for agentic robotics

Their framework has 3 layers:

- S2: foundation model + embodied harness. 
It's a decision center that interprets the goal, picks skills and tools, and checks outcomes
- S1: callable skills – VLA or WAM policies, object detection, motion planning, navigation
- S0: real-time body control – joints, balance, trajectory tracking

The S2 level is the most interesting for us now.

→ Foundation models provide knowledge and reasoning.
→ The embodied harness supplies everything around a model. It's basically an agent harness that works in the physical world.
It takes on the roles of context manager, tool and skill interface, planner, memory, and verifier. 
It determines what info reaches the model and what it can act on, how the system follows through on its decisions, and it maintains plans and memory.

text:
Do you know what connects Jakub’s proposal to a guessing game Claude Shannon ran in 1951?

Shannon asked people to guess the next letter in a piece of text. How many guesses it took helped him estimate how predictable English was. In the 1970s, Fred Jelinek’s team at IBM used a related measure, perplexity, to describe how hard a speech recognition task was.

What I find fascinating is that Jakub is still asking how well you can predict what comes next. This time, he wants the answer to help AI labs decide when to slow down.
name: The Turing Post
